# DC renderer robustness & performance hardening

## Context / Problem
The DC path shells out to pandoc per field. Three hazards from the DC experiment:
(1) subprocess tax — a flat ~0.3s/field spawn cost regardless of body size, and a
serial reconcile blocked ~20 min of wall time on `fork+exec`; (2) pathological-input
hang — one corpus body spun pandoc's jira reader 13.5 min at 95.8% CPU, and pypandoc
sets no timeout, so one field can stall the reconcile indefinitely; (3) pandoc is GPL
and rides in the wheel, so its provenance and licence must be pinned and recorded.

## Prior art / dependency boundaries (do NOT re-decide 271c's choices)
- **The renderer and its pandoc delivery are owned by 271c.** Story
  `[rebar:271c-e88f-3220-4c9b]` LANDED the pure renderer at
  `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` (merged `cf5155e528`), with pandoc from the
  pinned **`pypandoc-binary==1.15` wheel** via a `wiki` extra, so no system pandoc. This story hardens THAT module and pins THAT wheel; it adds no system
  pandoc and no `acli`-style version+sha binary pin.
- 271c leaves `WikiTextCodec` identity and `wiki_render.py` unreferenced by any codec op
  or live send path; all live wiring is the cutover story
  `[rebar:3388-96e8-e14e-4221]`'s and is **out of scope here**.
- The change-gated "no-op → no pandoc spawn" property is that cutover story's
  `rich_sha` gate, not on `origin/main` and not this story's to add. THIS story owns
  only cost, timeout, fallback, batching and compliance of a render that IS performed.

## Approach
- **Batch contiguous SAFE units to bound per-render subprocess cost.** Verified against
  the LANDED code (merged `cf5155e528`), not 271c's prose: `_lock_and_split`
  (`wiki_render.py:150`) returns `(kind, text)` pairs whose kinds are the module
  constants `_EXACT`/`_TABLE`/`_RENDER`/`_BLANK` (`:128-131`). This story groups each
  **maximal run of contiguous `_RENDER` units** into ONE pandoc document → one wiki
  segment, so many safe blocks cost one spawn per run, not one per unit. **A run
  ABSORBS interleaved `_BLANK` units**, re-emitting their exact text as the blank lines
  between blocks inside that document; a run breaks ONLY at a `_TABLE`/`_EXACT` unit.
  Load-bearing: the landed splitter emits a `_BLANK` between every pair of blocks
  (measured on `cf5155e528`), so if blanks broke a run no run of length >1 could exist
  and the batching would be a silent no-op. **No per-unit re-splitting of a batch's
  output**: the combined wiki is one segment; reassembly is at the run level. (The pinned wheel's pandoc
  **3.6.1** exposes no `--server`/daemon — verified absent from `--help` — so a
  persistent server is out of scope.)
- **Dangerous units are spliced VERBATIM — pandoc is never invoked on them.** A
  dangerous unit corrupts pandoc's jira reader, so it passes through unchanged at its
  original position. Order is restored by concatenating the ordered segments — no
  delimiter splitting, since each invocation renders one contiguous safe run.
- **Hard timeout + process-group reaping + batch-level verbatim fallback:** a plain
  `subprocess.run(timeout=)` reaps only the DIRECT child, so a pandoc jira-reader
  spinning at ~95.8% CPU (a pipe-holding grandchild) survives (bug d843, bpo-30154).
  So the renderer MUST NOT use pypandoc's high-level `convert_text`/`convert_file` API
  (no process handle); it locates pandoc via `pypandoc.get_pandoc_path()` and builds
  its OWN
  `subprocess.Popen([pandoc_path, …], start_new_session=True)`, **enforces the
  wall-clock timeout caller-side via `proc.communicate(timeout=dc_pandoc_timeout_s)`
  and, on `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, passes that `Popen`** to the leaf
  **`rebar._proc.reap_process_group`** (`_proc.py:26`) —
  `killpg` SIGTERM→grace→SIGKILL→bounded drain, already reused by the ACLI transport
  and grounding harness — killing the whole group, not just the direct child. It
  kills/drains only AFTER a timeout is detected, so caller-side detection is required
  (the `acli_subprocess.py` pattern). **The timeout is a config key**
  (`reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s`, default **10s**): >30× the observed ~0.3s/field
  render and ~80× below the 13.5-min hang; `grace`/`drain` reuse the ACLI caller's
  constants. On a safe-run call's timeout or non-zero exit, degrade **that entire
  segment** to its original Markdown verbatim (echo-safe) and record a **segment-level
  fallback marker**. The landed per-unit preservation check
  (`_render_unit`/`code_fragments`, `wiki_render.py:376-390`, `:266-288`) is LIFTED to
  the run: it runs over the run's combined source vs combined wiki, and a missing
  fragment degrades that whole run — the same boundary as a timeout or non-zero exit,
  including when pandoc exits 0. So segment boundary == fallback boundary for all three
  failure modes and no unit inside a run can be silently corrupted; other segments and the verbatim dangerous units are unaffected.
  The fallback boundary is exactly the pandoc-invocation boundary.
- **Compliance:** pin the wheel, create a repo-root `NOTICE` recording pandoc's GPL
  entry, and verify the pin in CI.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira_family/wiki_render.py` — own `subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True)`
  over `pypandoc.get_pandoc_path()`, per-invocation timeout +
  `rebar._proc.reap_process_group`, safe-run batching, verbatim dangerous units,
  run-level preservation check and fallback (all as above).
- `pyproject.toml` — pin the `pypandoc-binary` wheel version (extends 271c's pin).
- config (`reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s`, default 10s). A `reconciler.*` key has a
  fixed multi-file surface (mirrors `reconciler.jira_cli_timeout`); update together:
  `_config_schema.py` — field `dc_pandoc_timeout_s: float = 10.0` on `ReconcilerConfig`
  + validator `_as_float(v, k, minimum=0.0)`; `_config_sources.py` — a
  `_CANONICAL_ENV_NAMES` alias only if a non-derived env name is wanted (else
  auto-derived `REBAR_RECONCILER_DC_PANDOC_TIMEOUT_S`);
  `tests/golden/config_surface.json` — deliberately REGENERATE (the guard
  `tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py` is removal-only, so it will NOT flag a new
  key's omission); `docs/config.md` — document it under `[tool.rebar.reconciler]`. A
  unit test mirrors `test_config_file_wiring.py`'s four-consumer pattern.
- CI workflow — verify the wheel pin.
- **`NOTICE` (NEW file, repo root)** — the repo has only `LICENSE` today and no
  SBOM/notice artifact, so this story CREATES `NOTICE` and records the wheel-bundled
  pandoc's GPL entry (name + version 3.6.1 + license + upstream) there.
- `tests/` — timeout, fallback, and batching tests over the vendored DC corpus.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every pandoc invocation runs under a caller-side wall-clock timeout via
  `proc.communicate(timeout=dc_pandoc_timeout_s)` (config
  `reconciler.dc_pandoc_timeout_s`, default 10s — above the ~0.3s normal render, below
  the 13.5-min hang) and, on `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, process-group reaping via
  `rebar._proc.reap_process_group` (the CPU-spinning grandchild is killed,
  not orphaned); on timeout or non-zero exit it degrades that safe-run segment
  to verbatim Markdown without raising and the render returns; verified by
  `test_dc_pandoc_timeout_falls_back` (asserts the group is reaped) and
  `test_dc_pandoc_error_degrades`.
- [ ] A changed body of N contiguous safe units renders in one pandoc invocation (one
  wiki segment) with original block order preserved, dangerous units are spliced
  VERBATIM with no pandoc call, and a safe-run timeout degrades exactly that run's
  segment (segment boundary == fallback boundary); verified by
  `test_dc_render_batches_safe_run`, `test_dc_dangerous_unit_verbatim_no_pandoc`, and
  `test_dc_segment_fallback_boundary`.
- [ ] The pandoc binary comes from the `pypandoc-binary` wheel pinned by version in
  `pyproject.toml` (271c's mechanism, not a system pandoc) and the pin is verified in
  CI; verified by the CI wheel-pin check.
- [ ] The wheel-bundled pandoc's GPL licence is recorded in a NEW repo-root `NOTICE`
  file (only `LICENSE` exists today), naming pandoc, version 3.6.1 and its licence;
  verified by `tests/unit/test_notice_records_pandoc_gpl.py`.
